full_judgment: 5. In this connection it may be mentioned that in the impugned decision of the Tribunal it was observed that the Arbitration Court was not properly constituted since it was not available on record as to whether the Arbitration Court consisted of three members including a Chairman as contemplated under Article 4 of P.O. 13 of 1972. Whether the Arbitration Court was properly constituted or not with three members at the minimum is a question of fact which could only be ascertained on proper evidence. There could not be a presumption that in the absence of anything else to the contrary it could be assumed that the Arbitration Court was not properly constituted unless such finding could be made on consideration of proper evidence in that regard. In this connection, it may be further observed that the proceeding before the Arbitration Court was an ex parte one and the respondent No. 2 was not present before the Arbitration Court. The respondent No. 2, however, duly appeared before the Thana Magistrate when a further enquiry was held on the dispute. Respondent No. 2 did not raise any objection before the Thana Magistrate about the improper constitution of the Arbitration Court.
